key_insight: By engineering film morphology, the authors enabled the first robust lateral electrical and magnetotransport measurements in chiral 2D perovskite R-(MBA)2PbI4.
engineering_relevance: This shows that microstructure control can unlock device-level characterization and future spintronic integration for chiral perovskites.
method: Optimized thin-film morphology of R-(MBA)2PbI4 for in-plane transport.
Fabricated Hall-bar devices for dark Hall and magnetoresistance measurements.
Compared transport paths with and without grain-boundary crossings.
evidence_signal: Hall measurements revealed p-type conduction with ~0.2 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 mobility and ~3×10^14 cm^-2 carrier density, and magnetoresistance increased when paths crossed grain boundaries.
watch_item: The reported in-plane mobility is still very low, so morphology improvements and contact/grain-boundary effects may strongly limit practical device performance.
paper_title: Morphology control and low-temperature magnetotransport in chiral 2D perovskite R-(MBA)$_2$PbI$_4$
